data.narrative:
Stardust Solutions is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised $75M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of nine private peers in Climate & Energy (including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen) and one public comparable (LNZA), though a sufficiently tight peer set at the same stage and valuation tier was not available for median-based triangulation.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable approach. Using total capital raised ($75M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to next-stage progression, this method implies a $150M post-money valuation. The Peer-Median method was not applied because the broader Climate & Energy universe lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting clustering criteria; deploying all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $128M (low) to $172M (high), centered on $150M. This median reflects a reasonable step-up from the capital base but remains subject to material uncertainties: the single-method reliance limits robustness, and the fragmented peer set in frontier-tech climate ventures means comparable multiples are sparse. Key unknowns include Stardust's unit economics, capital efficiency relative to peers, and technology maturity stage within Series A.
